summary: Extracted the first-run setup-wizard completion flag (previously near-identical copy-pasted services in mymatasan and myidsan) into one canonical domain/shared/services.ISetupStateService and domain/shared/apis.SetupHandlers pair, then used that seam to bring every app in the suite up to wizard parity: myseliasan gained a first-run wizard it never had (welcome, import a myidsan SSO bundle and save it, first site, adopt a node, handover to a real superadmin, done), myiotsan's onboarding wizard was promoted off a per-browser localStorage flag onto the same server-side setup.state row so dismissal now sticks per install rather than per browser (and its enrol/ready steps now show live enrollment-window and quarantine-candidate state instead of describing them abstractly), and myidsan's wizard gained a 4th step, "Where sessions live", that reads, live-tests, and saves the storage.cache settings section in place. The shared service also picked up myidsan's stricter insert guard (row == nil || row.Id == 0) as the canonical behavior, since mymatasan's original copy lacked it and would have silently persisted nothing against a repo that signals "missing" via a zero-value row rather than an error.
compatibility: No schema change — the flag continues to live under RuntimeSetting key setup.state, the same row every app already read/wrote. Existing installs that already completed setup on any app are unaffected (the flag round-trips unchanged); an existing myseliasan install with no prior wizard simply starts offering one to its next superadmin login until dismissed or completed. myiotsan installs lose their old localStorage-based dismissal (a one-time re-prompt is expected on next login until an admin dismisses/completes the wizard server-side); the wizard's own emptiness gate (device count) is unchanged, so an established hub with devices already enrolled never sees it regardless. myidsan's new wizard step is purely additive and fully skippable; skipping it leaves the existing single-instance in-process cache default, identical to pre-change behavior.
